name: DragSwitch
summary: A red frame sits on one face of the polyhedron; left-hand pinch-drags move it to the adjacent face in the drag's direction, and a right-hand pinch selects the framed face.
howItWorks: The next face is the neighbour whose centre best matches the hand's drag direction. It was among the three best techniques, with the fewest errors on small polyhedra, and was rated highly on complex models. Tested with 16 participants selecting single faces on regular polyhedra (4, 6 or 12 faces, two sizes) with tracked hands.
limitations: Many steps to reach distant faces.

relationships.note: Introduced with seven other face-selection techniques in the same study.
The study's baseline (DragRotate) rotates the object with one hand and selects with a hand ray.
